title: Rainfall-associated expansion of frog active communities is more boundary-biased than uniform activation predicts
rc11_additions: A prefrozen same-observer robustness analysis using public NAAMP ObserverTrackingID.
An explicit limitation that a species-specific activation-shift null remains untested.
frozen_core_claims: Recent-rain conditions are associated with expansion of the behaviourally realized acoustic community across active spatial footprint, local alpha richness and route gamma richness in NAAMP.
Active-unit taxonomic depth has the same recent-rain direction in the aligned NAAMP and FrogID analyses; this is cross-dataset consistency, not independent validation or a pooled effect-size claim.
The North American four-component incidence allocation strongly rejects the original magnitude-matched uniform-activation null under kappa 1, 2 and 5.
The allocation also strongly rejects the persistence-preserving uniform-activation stress test at dry-state anchor weights 0.50, 0.75 and 0.90.
The boundary-biased allocation and all three headline expansion coefficients persist in the large same-observer subset.
Pairwise Sorensen change remains secondary bounded context rather than the structural discovery.
frozen_interpretation: Rainfall-associated expansion enters the behaviourally realized frog community more strongly across spatial and taxonomic boundaries than uniform activation predicts; the pattern survives strong dry-state persistence and restriction to surveys made by the same recorded observer.
frozen_negative_boundaries: No rainfall causality, occupancy, abundance, colonization, extinction or demographic-recruitment claim.
No independent-validation or worldwide-universality claim from FrogID.
No unique biological mechanism identified by uniform-null rejection.
No claim that observers are interchangeable.
No claim that the same-observer restriction removes all detectability bias.
No claim that species-specific activation heterogeneity has been excluded.
The species-specific activation-shift null is explicitly reserved and untested.
Activation geometry remains falsified as a rainfall-specific species trait.
No title-level homogenization claim and no confirmatory Sorensen-equivalence claim.

species_specific_activation_null.purpose: Test whether allowing species-specific rainfall-response shifts alone can reproduce the observed boundary allocation.
